title: NEXUS Chest CT Decision Instrument
aliases: chest CT vs chest x-ray trauma
sources: Rodriguez RM et al. PLoS Med 2015 (NEXUS Chest CT); JAMA Surg 2015
purpose: In blunt trauma patients ≥ 14 years imaged within 6 hours of injury, identifies who can safely skip chest CT. If ALL seven criteria are absent, clinically major thoracic injury is effectively excluded.

items.label: Abnormal chest X-ray (any thoracic injury or widened mediastinum)
Rapid deceleration mechanism (fall > 20 ft / 6 m, or MVC > 40 mph / 64 kph with sudden deceleration)

interpretation.label: No criteria — very low risk. Chest CT can be safely omitted (sensitivity ~ 99% for major injury; ~ 95% for minor injury)
≥ 1 criterion — not low risk. Chest CT is reasonable, especially if an abnormal CXR or a high-risk mechanism is present. Use the CXR result and clinical judgement to choose CT vs. CXR-only

notes: Two versions exist: NEXUS Chest (CXR decision, uses a similar list) and NEXUS Chest CT (this one). 'Major' injury = aortic/great-vessel injury, rupture of a bronchus/diaphragm/oesophagus, haemopneumothorax needing a tube, ≥ 3 rib fractures, pulmonary contusion, sternal fracture with associated injury. The rule reduces CT use by ~ 25–37% depending on setting.
buildNote: Rule — any positive criterion → not low-risk.
